dispositions.G1_CLOSED_WIDER_THAN_THE_CASE: A non-numeric count is a clean defect again. Verified beyond the shipped case: entries as a string, as null, as a list and as a dict all produce 'cites ... entries, but its head is entry N of ...' and no exception. The mutant that swallows the failure and accepts the count silently is killed by the shipped case.
dispositions.G2_CLOSED: test_a_truncated_head_does_not_resolve_by_prefix kills the startswith mutant on the cited-head lookup, which is the mutant pass 1 named and pass 2 found still alive. It is dead.
dispositions.G3_CLOSED_FOR_WHAT_WAS_RAISED: Every state pass 2 listed is now refused except one: an address of another node, a substring node, a missing address and an invented filename all earn defects. The 2026-09-06 report is legitimately resolved and I checked it directly rather than by reading the code: its address is not in heads, it declares node:local, its filename 23d3b48086be.json equals its own head[:12], and _cited_export returns the current export with no refusal. Two narrow residuals and one by-design limit remain; see H4, H5 and the note on C4.
dispositions.G4_PARTLY_AND_THE_COVERAGE_CLAIM_IS_FALS: The collapse is a good shape: after the address-node comparison the two values are provably equal, so one comparison is better than two. But the second comparison is not gone - it moved from node ids to directory names - and both containment mutants are reachable by cases. See H1 and H2, which carry the two case bodies.

findings.H1_the_T3_case_is_still_in_the_harmless_: test_a_declared_node_must_equal_the_nodes_name_and_not_merely_contain_it declares node:loc against a node:local export. Under the containment mutant _node_id_of(_export_node(address)) not in node, 'node:local' is not in 'node:loc', so the mutant still refuses and the case still passes: the mutant survives the shipped suite. The killing direction is a declared node that CONTAINS the real one. Changing node:loc to node:local-2 in that same case kills it, verified. No second node is needed. This is the second pass in a row where a coverage claim ran ahead of the fixture, and it is the same direction error the commit message says was caught and rerun.
findings.H2_the_remaining_comparison_is_reachable: The comment and the commit say one comparison remains that no case can reach while the registry holds a single node. It is reachable. The node layer pins node_id to the registry's single SELF, which is why building the second node through it fails; building it one level below, with RecordService and ConsoleService told a second node id, produces a chain the export replays, and pointing journal.NODE_REGISTRY at a two-node registry puts both exports in heads. Naming matters: the wrong candidate must sort first under a containment reading, so the nodes must be node:loc and node:local, not node:local and node:local-2. With that, the mutant _export_node(path) in _export_node(address) resolves a node:local citation to node:loc's export and the case fails. Verified: control passes unmutated, mutant killed. The case body is in the witness record.
findings.H3_the_filename_check_is_pinned_in_one_d: The mutant that compares the address by endswith instead of by exact basename survives both the shipped suite and my cases. An address whose basename is xx<head12>.json would pass under it. The shipped code is right; nothing pins it. One case with a prefixed basename closes it.
findings.H4_a_live_address_may_still_contradict_i: The early return on address in heads happens before any node comparison, so a report naming the current export while declaring a node that has no export passes with no defect. Carried unchanged from pass 2's B4. Nothing is misdirected, because the address is correct and authoritative; what passes unremarked is a false node field in a report, which is the one field whose whole purpose is to be checked.
findings.H5_everything_above_the_node_directory_i: _export_node reads only the second-to-last directory, so an address missing the nodes/ prefix, or under an invented parent, resolves: node-local/journal/<head12>.json and ../../elsewhere/node-local/journal/<head12>.json both pass. A reader following either lands nowhere. Worth noting that after this repair the address is fully derivable from node and head, so a single equality against nodes/<node dir>/journal/<head[:12]>.json would replace three comparisons and close H4 and H5 at once. The test harness uses absolute addresses, so that shape would need the fixtures to move to repository-relative ones.

observed.by_design_limit_recorded_not_faulted: An address whose filename is the cited head's prefix but which was never exported cannot be told from a genuinely superseded export, because the gate cannot know at which heads a node was exported. Verified: such a citation passes. That is the honest boundary of the pin and not a defect; the pin is what stops a fabricated address from naming anything the node never reached.
observed.boundary_reading_on_F5: Sound. open_office records grants through ConsoleService.grant, whose payload authority.grant_payload owns, so adding the direction to that payload changes a shape the Console Service records and crosses into that contract. The alternative of appending a separate entry from the node layer does not obviously avoid the crossing either: a new record_kind is vocabulary CLASSIFICATION.md owns. Naming it and not taking it is the right call, and the report now says so in the object it concerns.
